UnitStatement: OpenPipeStress is a proposed free/open-source, code-neutral piping stress analysis platform implementing open global piping flexibility mechanics with a GUI and reporting workflow.
OpenPipeStress requires users to supply governing code data, material properties, component data, SIFs/flexibility factors, allowables, and rule-pack checks.

The decomposition incorporates a formal SOFTWARE_DECOMP review against PRD.md and INTENT.md plus the v0.3 architecture-runway amendment accepted by the human project authority on 2026-04-30 as the current downstream basis.

The v0.3 amendment adds PKG-00 Software Architecture Runway as a pre-workflow gate defining the product/software spine (GUI, backend, persistence, schemas, diagnostics, APIs, jobs, tests) before Type 2 implementation across PKG-01 through PKG-12.

Revision v0.4 records SCA-001, authorizing PKG-00 SEMANTIC_READY content as an architecture-basis candidate for sealed brief injection without treating PKG-00 as ISSUED, and resolves selected stack/runtime/schema/persistence/test TBDs.

Revision v0.5 records SCA-002, admitting OpenPipeStress_PRD_v0.2 as the working basis for a schema-backed piping design engine and stress-model authoring environment, adding coverage for physical design knowledge, constraints, model operations, immutable model states, analysis runs, comparison, handoff, and external-prover boundaries.

Revision v0.6 records SCA-003, resolving the MVP physical package/container decision as a local SQLite-backed project store and index profile with rebuildable retrieval sidecars, preserving JSON Schema 2020-12, JCS-compatible hashes, deterministic round-trip, local-first privacy, and no-bypass boundaries.

Revision v0.7 records SCA-004, adding PKG-17 Export Format Interoperability and making deterministic export packages, profiles, stable ID maps, loss reports, CAEPIPE MBF validation, stress-neutral CSV/JSON, conservative PCF, GLB/glTF review geometry, and export adapter SDK explicit while preserving no-bundled-solver, no-proprietary-example, no-reverse-engineering, no-license-bypass, and no-compliance-claim constraints.

The decomposition intentionally separates open mechanics from protected standards/code data; mechanics solved from user-rule checked from human professional approval; and global centerline analysis from specialized local FEA handoff.

SOW-001: The project shall produce a source-available noncommercial piping stress analysis platform.
SOW-002: The software shall remain code-neutral: the solver computes mechanics and user-supplied rule packs evaluate acceptability.
SOW-003: The public repository shall not redistribute protected standards text, tables, figures, examples, material allowables, SIF tables, flexibility-factor tables, or protected dimensional tables.
SOW-004: The system shall require users to supply code-specific and project-specific data needed for code checks.
SOW-005: The analytical core shall model piping as a 3D centerline/frame system with six degrees of freedom per node.
SOW-006: The solver shall implement straight pipe elements with open mechanics section and stiffness calculations.
SOW-007: The component model shall support bends and elbows with user-entered SIFs, flexibility factors, and bend geometry.
SOW-008: The component model shall support branch connections with user-entered reinforcement, SIF, flexibility, and local data fields.
SOW-009: The component model shall support rigid and semi-rigid valves, flanges, reducers, and specialty items using user-supplied dimensions, weights, and centers of gravity.
SOW-010: The component model shall support expansion joints using manufacturer/user-supplied stiffness, effective area, movement limits, and hardware data.
SOW-011: The solver shall support anchors, guides, line stops, vertical supports, springs, and imposed displacements.
SOW-012: The solver shall support nonlinear support behavior such as one-way restraints, lift-off, gaps, and friction through a controlled iterative method.
SOW-013: The analysis engine shall support primitive load cases for weight, pressure, thermal expansion, imposed displacement, hydrotest, wind, seismic, and occasional loads.
SOW-014: The analysis engine shall support unit-aware load-case algebra and user-defined combinations.
SOW-015: The stress module shall recover fundamental mechanics stresses from forces, moments, pressure, and section properties.
SOW-016: The product shall provide a private rule-pack schema for user-defined stress checks, allowables, formulas, and pass/fail criteria.
SOW-017: The product shall support private material libraries with temperature-dependent properties, allowables, and provenance fields.
SOW-018: The product shall support private pipe section and component libraries with provenance and redistribution status.
SOW-019: The public project shall accept component data only when provenance and redistribution rights are documented.
SOW-020: The GUI shall provide a 3D centerline modeler with model tree and piping component visualization.
SOW-021: The GUI shall provide editors for materials, sections, components, load cases, supports, rule packs, and private libraries.
SOW-022: The GUI shall distinguish data required for solving from data required for code checking and shall block/qualify results when required data is missing.
SOW-023: The GUI shall provide results review for displacements, rotations, forces, moments, restraint reactions, equipment loads, stresses, and ratios.
SOW-024: The product shall generate auditable calculation reports including inputs, sources, warnings, assumptions, results, rule-pack checksums, and limitations.
SOW-025: All calculations, schemas, imports, exports, and rule evaluations shall be unit-aware.
SOW-026: The project shall maintain verification benchmarks, regression tests, and numerical quality checks for solver and stress recovery behavior.
SOW-027: The project shall maintain a validation manual that distinguishes mechanics verification from code compliance and professional signoff.
SOW-028: The repository shall include contributor governance, IP controls, and review procedures preventing copyrighted standards data from entering the public project.
SOW-029: The product shall be local-first and shall protect private rule packs, private material data, private component data, and project models.
SOW-030: The architecture shall support public APIs, plugins, and import/export adapters for integration with external tools.
SOW-031: The product shall support optional handoff of selected local-detail problems to external shell/solid FEA workflows.
SOW-032: The project shall provide reproducible build, packaging, and CI/CD workflows for supported platforms.
SOW-033: The project shall provide user/developer documentation and invented-data examples for education and testing.
SOW-034: The product shall preserve professional responsibility boundaries: agents/software do not certify, approve, seal, or declare engineering code compliance for reliance.
SOW-035: The solver shall be designed for sparse numerical performance and reproducible results on practical piping models.
SOW-036: The GUI and reports shall support baseline accessibility and usability appropriate for engineering review.
SOW-037: Telemetry, if implemented, shall be opt-in, privacy-preserving, and shall not transmit private project/code data.
SOW-038: The software architecture shall be extensible without allowing plugins/adapters to bypass governance, unit safety, or data-boundary constraints.
SOW-039: The product shall produce reproducibility artifacts such as model hashes, solver version, rule-pack checksum, and input manifest.
SOW-040: The product shall implement private data handling controls, including redaction/export safeguards where reports or shared models may expose protected/private values.
SOW-041: The project shall define machine-readable project, model, material, component, load, result, and report schemas.
SOW-042: Rule packs shall be versioned, source-noted, checksum-addressed, and explicitly marked for redistribution status.
SOW-043: The report system shall prohibit automatic inclusion of protected code text, copied standards tables, or proprietary formulas in generated public reports/templates.
SOW-044: The product shall provide import mechanisms that record source/provenance/license metadata for component and material data.
SOW-045: The rule-pack evaluator shall be sandboxed and unit-aware, not arbitrary executable code.
SOW-046: The product shall support result exports suitable for review, regression comparison, and downstream tooling.
SOW-047: The product shall clearly distinguish mechanics solved, rule-pack checked, and professionally code-compliant/human-approved states.
SOW-048: The project shall define project license, governance, release, and maintainer policies.
SOW-049: The project shall define criteria for when global beam analysis is sufficient and when local shell/solid analysis handoff is needed.
SOW-050: The product shall support create/open/save/versioned project persistence with deterministic round-trip serialization of models, units, loads, rule-pack references, and provenance metadata.
SOW-051: The product shall calculate pipe section and mass properties from user-entered dimensions and material data with unit checks.
SOW-052: The load engine shall support concentrated forces, concentrated moments, and distributed user loads in addition to core primitive piping load categories.
SOW-053: The solver shall detect and report singular, ill-conditioned, and nonconverged analysis states with deterministic diagnostics.
SOW-054: The project shall provide a headless command-line or structured I/O analysis runner for early solver verification, regression, and automation.
SOW-055: The GUI shall keep solve execution reviewable with background solve execution, progress, cancellation, and diagnostic presentation.
SOW-056: The project shall select and record implementation stack, runtime, GUI framework, solver-library, and packaging target decisions before implementation work proceeds.
SOW-057: The project shall define repository/module architecture, ownership boundaries, dependency rules, and layer responsibilities before package-level implementation proceeds.

SOW-058: The project shall define application-service command, query, background job, cancellation, and transaction boundaries between GUI, headless runner, domain core, solver, storage, and reporting.
SOW-059: The project shall define persistence format, schema-versioning, migration, canonicalization, and deterministic round-trip strategy before project-file implementation proceeds.
SOW-060: The project shall define GUI state, editing, selection, undo/redo, viewport integration, and user workflow architecture before GUI feature slices proceed.

SOW-061: The project shall define diagnostics, warning classes, errors, result envelopes, and user-facing/machine-readable failure contracts across solver, rule packs, GUI, CLI, reports, and adapters.
SOW-062: The project shall define public and internal API boundaries between GUI, application services, domain core, solver, storage, reporting, private libraries, plugins, and adapters.
SOW-063: The project shall define layered software test strategy and acceptance gates for architecture, schemas, services, solver, GUI, CLI, reports, packaging, security, and regressions.
SOW-064: The product shall be scoped as an analysis-grade piping design engine and stress-model authoring environment with a full internal solver and non-authoritative professional reliance boundary.

SOW-065: The schema-backed physical model shall be the source of truth for editable piping design data, including geometry, components, supports, equipment interfaces, loads, constraints, provenance, unresolved assumptions, and warnings.

SOW-066: The product shall transform the physical model into a solver-ready analytical model deterministically and record transformation warnings when physical design data cannot be represented analytically.

SOW-067: The product shall support user-supplied design knowledge such as endpoints, line data, routing corridors, no-go volumes, supportable zones, equipment interfaces, access constraints, slope/drain/vent requirements, and owner/project metadata.

SOW-068: The constraint system shall validate available design knowledge for connectivity, route, clearance, support-zone, slope/drain/vent conflicts, and missing required data with provenance-aware messages.

SOW-069: All GUI and agent edits shall be represented as structured model operations that pass schema validation, constraint validation, diff preview, and controlled application through the model engine.
SOW-070: Accepted model operations shall preserve operation history, rationale, assumptions, affected entities, and audit metadata needed for reproducible model-state review.
SOW-071: The product shall save named immutable model states with tags, notes, external references, unresolved assumptions, warnings, and deterministic hashes.

SOW-072: The product shall save analysis runs bound to exact model states, solver versions, settings, units, load cases, diagnostics, results, rule-pack references, library references, and result hashes.
SOW-073: The product shall compare two model states and/or two analysis runs deterministically using stable IDs, manual mappings where required, unit-normalized result deltas, and tolerance profiles.

SOW-074: The product shall generate schema-compliant handoff packages with model hash, units manifest, entity IDs, library/rule references, unresolved assumptions, warnings, target mapping metadata, and unsupported-target flags.

SOW-075: The product shall support external-prover workflow metadata without forcing a formal prover-status lifecycle, automatic professional acceptance record, or comprehensive commercial-tool result ingestion in the MVP.

SOW-076: The GUI shall support design-authoring and comparison workflows, including design knowledge panels, constraint/warning panels, state/run browsers, comparison tables, and graphical comparison overlays.
